tests.name: Dynamics
tests.task: Each question has a written part and a drawing. Together they contain all the information needed to answer.

items.q: Which ball is heaviest?
items.x: Weight cannot necessarily be deduced from size.

items.q: Three rubber wheels, A, B and C are touching so that if one moves the others must also move. If wheel A turns clockwise, which way will wheel C turn?
items.x: A causes B to move anti-clockwise, which in turn causes C to rotate clockwise.

items.q: A section through a dam is shown. At which point is the dam strongest?
items.x: The dam must be strongest at C where it is withstanding the greatest pressure.

items.q: In the same dam, at which point is the water coldest?
items.x: At C as temperature decreases with depth.

items.q: The beam is twice as thick at one end as the other. At what point can it be placed on the wall, and at a right angle to the wall, so that it balances?
items.x: Although A is the middle of the beam, it will be heavier on one side. Relative volumes and their weights seem best balanced at B.

items.q: When rays of light hit a lens, in which direction do they continue?
items.x: As rays of light hit the surface they will be turned to move through the lens at an angle 90 degrees to the surface, roughly in the direction indicated by arrow B. However, when the light moving through the lens hits the outer surface it will emerge at an angle 90 degrees to the surface of the lens, roughly in the direction of arrow A.

items.q: A band passes around all the wheels so that they can all be turned by the driving wheel. When the driving wheel turns clockwise, which way does wheel W turn?
items.x: The wheels all turn clockwise apart from the wheel in the middle where the band passes in a contra direction.

items.q: The drawing shows a cross-section of a wall, with a shelf upright against it. By means of a hinge, the shelf can be folded upright against the wall. It can be let down to the horizontal, being held at point H by a rope, which is suspended from a hook, A, B or C. When the shelf is let down and supported by the rope, which hook is least likely to be pulled out of the wall?
items.x: Hooking at A gives the slightest angle between the rope and the wall so that, because the ‘pull’ of the rope is more downwards rather than outwards at A than it would be at B or C, A is least likely to be pulled out.

items.q: If the three iron bars are all the same length, which one will support the greatest weight?
items.x: Although having less height than A or width than C, the section of B has the greater overall surface and its section is least likely to bend or twist either vertically or horizontally.

items.q: Three racing cars travel at equal speed round the built-up curve of a bend. Which car is most likely to slip?
items.x: If they entered the curve at the same speed, car 3 would emerge at the end of the curve in front of 2, which would be in front of 1, because car 3 travels the shortest distance. It is therefore most likely to slip on the bend especially as it receives least corresponding pressure from the bank.

items.q: If three racing cars are level with each other, side by side as they go into the bend, and all are also level as they come out of the bend, which car is travelling fastest?
items.x: Car 1 has travelled furthest and therefore fastest.

items.q: This old-fashioned ‘grandfather clock’ pendulum and weight are made of iron. To keep correct time, in which direction might the weight need to be adjusted in summer?
items.x: The effect of heat upon iron is to make it expand so that the pendulum will swing more slowly in summer, so that the weight will need to be moved upwards during the summer to maintain regularity of beat.

items.q: To lever up the large, heavy weight with the least effort, by pushing down in the direction of the arrow, at which point under the beam should the block be placed?
items.x: Greatest leverage will be obtained by placing the block at point 1.

items.q: A heavy metal bar is fixed inside a cardboard tube. When the tube is placed on a slope, as shown, which direction will the tube roll?
items.x: The weight of the bar acting in a vertically downward direction will make the tube roll up the slope.

items.q: When the driving wheel 1 turns in the direction shown, wheel 2 turns …
items.x: The band moves around the surface of 2 in the same direction as 1.

items.q: Assuming that the belt and wheels did not jam, which wheel would turn fastest?
items.x: Wheel 2 turns fastest as it is the smallest circle (or cog) around which the band passes.

items.q: Two cars, A and B, one travelling from the north, N, due south, S, and the other from the west, W, due east, E, collide at point P. They come to rest in the region of south east, as shown. If the slower car was travelling exactly at the speed limit, which car was probably breaking the speed limit?
items.x: The cars have been pushed further south than east so that car B must have had the greater force or speed.

items.q: The ladders, 1 and 2, and the walls are viewed from the side. Which ladder is safer when climbed?
items.x: As the base of the ladder moves away from the vertical the less any weight is pushed safely into the ground.

items.q: In a hot-water cylinder, from which outlet should hot water be taken?
items.x: Hot water rises so that hot water is best drawn from the top of the cylinder. 3 is a marginally better answer than 4 because this would ensure the best flow of water through the cylinder.

items.q: When the spacecraft is not affected by the Earth’s gravity, and the thrust of the rocket is zero, the astronaut will:

ot: stay where he is at side 2
be thrust towards the nose at 3

items.x: Without any gravitational forces the astronaut continues in the same position and at the same speed as the craft.

items.q: In space, when the stationary vehicle accelerates, the spaceman will:

ot: be thrust towards the nose at 3
float upwards, due to weightlessness, towards 2
fall on his head on the floor at side 4

items.x: Upon acceleration, it is only the craft that moves, whilst the spaceman will only begin to move when he encounters and is then propelled by the floor of the craft.

items.q: When wheel 1 turns clockwise, which way does wheel 4 turn?
items.x: After wheel 1, the second wheel turns in the opposite direction, because the band connecting the two wheels has been crossed. The third wheel moves in the same direction as wheel 2, because the bands go the same way around both wheels. As the bands are crossed between wheels 3 and 4, wheel 4 will turn in the opposite direction to wheel 3, therefore clockwise.

items.q: In which direction does a steel ball continue after impact on a rigid, heavy steel block?
items.x: As both items are steel and the block is rigid, the direction of the ball is likely to be almost equal and opposite to the direction of its impact, therefore 4.

items.q: In which direction will ball 3 move when ball 1 is struck as shown?
items.x: Ball 1 will strike ball 2 driving it at an angle of about 45 degrees to hit ball 3 at approximately the same angle making an angle of 90 degrees so that ball 3 continues horizontally in the same direction as the first ball.

items.q: Which way will helical gear H turn when helical gear M turns as shown?
items.x: Gear M causes H to move in a contrary direction to itself so that, if in the diagram M is rotating clockwise H will rotate anti-clockwise as B

tests.name: Tracing
tests.task: Follow each line from the left-hand side of the page to the symbol where it ends. Find that symbol in the chart at the top and choose the letter underneath it.
